newsitem.title: UK: Crowd violent halts Northern Ireland soccer match.
newsitem.headline: Crowd violent halts Northern Ireland soccer match.

text.p: Protestant soccer fans attacked buses carrying Catholic supporters of a rival club in Northern Ireland on Saturday and crowd violence halted the match at half-time.

Police said several fans and policemen were hurt in fights before and during the match between Cliftonville, from a predominantly Roman Catholic area of Belfast, and mainly Protestant Portadown, 25 miles (40 km) southwest of the Northern Ireland capital.
Full details were not immediately available. Portadown was trailing 0-1 when the game was abandoned at half-time.
Two buses carrying Cliftonville supporters to Portadown's Shamrock Park ground came under attack from Portadown fans who shattered windows of the vehicles, police said.
Last month Cliftonville fans were prevented by Protestants from reaching the the Oval ground for a cup tie in East Belfast.
Two of their matches this season have been brought forward because of concern about possible violence in the charged atmosphere pervading Northern Ireland.
The province has been on edge since sectarian violence flared in July and August over the holding of Protstant Orange Order parades.
The bombing of Britain's Northern Ireland army base by Irish Republican Army guerrillas two weeks ago has also raised tension.
